name: Shannon theory in quantum key distribution
summary: QKD security and channel capacities are written in entropies inherited from Shannon. The BB84 key rate uses the binary entropy h(Q), and the Holevo bound and quantum relative entropy generalize classical mutual information.

name: Integrability, GGE and the quantum Newton's cradle
summary: Bethe-ansatz-integrable systems such as the Lieb–Liniger gas have extensively many conserved charges and do not thermalize to a Gibbs state. Trapped 1D Bose gases (the quantum Newton's cradle, Tonks–Girardeau gases) showed this, and the steady state is a generalized Gibbs ensemble.
sources: Kinoshita, Wenger & Weiss (2006). "A quantum Newton's cradle". *Nature* 440, 900. [doi:10.1038/nature04693](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04693)
Kinoshita, Wenger & Weiss (2004). "Observation of a One-Dimensional Tonks-Girardeau Gas". *Science* 305, 1125. [doi:10.1126/science.1100700](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1100700)

Lieb & Liniger (1963). "Exact Analysis of an Interacting Bose Gas. I. The General Solution and the Ground State". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 1605. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.1605](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.1605)

name: Blackbody radiation shift in optical clocks
summary: The ambient Planck field Stark-shifts clock transitions by an amount ∝T⁴. It is a leading systematic of optical lattice clocks and has driven cryogenic clocks with fractional BBR uncertainty near 10^{-20}.
sources: Hassan et al. (2025). "Cryogenic Optical Lattice Clock with 1.7×10^{-20} Blackbody Radiation Stark Uncertainty". [arXiv:2506.05304](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05304)

name: Bose–Einstein condensation from quantum statistics to atoms
summary: The BEC critical temperature from Bose–Einstein statistics, nλ³=ζ(3/2), was realized in 1995 in dilute alkali gases. Trapped gases modify the density of states (T_c∝N^{1/3}ω) but test the same counting.
sources: Dalfovo et al. (1998). "Theory of Bose-Einstein condensation in trapped gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 71, 463. [arXiv:cond-mat/9806038](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9806038)

name: Indistinguishability and the symmetrization postulate
summary: Bose and Fermi statistics follow from the symmetrization postulate for identical particles, and Gibbs' 1/N! (the resolution of the mixing paradox) is its classical limit. Thermal states are density operators ρ=e^{-βH}/Z in the postulates' formalism.

name: Thermal light: Bose–Einstein photon statistics
summary: A single mode of blackbody radiation has a Bose–Einstein (geometric) photon-number distribution with variance n̄²+n̄, which is the origin of Hanbury Brown–Twiss bunching g²(0)=2. Coherent states are Poissonian, so photon statistics distinguish thermal from laser light.
sources: Glauber (1963). "Coherent and Incoherent States of the Radiation Field". *Phys. Rev.* 131, 2766. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.131.2766](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.131.2766)

name: Classical and quantum non-equilibrium dynamics
summary: Master equations, linear response and fluctuation theorems carry over from classical stochastic systems to open and closed quantum many-body systems. The Lindblad equation is the quantum Markov master equation.

name: KPZ superdiffusion in quantum spin chains
summary: Infinite-temperature spin transport in the isotropic Heisenberg chain is superdiffusive with z=3/2, and the spin profile matches the KPZ scaling function. This was observed with a quantum gas microscope.
breaks: Classical KPZ comes from a noisy, non-integrable growth equation. In the integrable Heisenberg chain the higher moments of the transferred magnetization deviate from Tracy–Widom, so only part of the KPZ phenomenology carries over.
sources: Ljubotina, Žnidarič & Prosen (2019). "Kardar-Parisi-Zhang Physics in the Quantum Heisenberg Magnet". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 210602. [arXiv:1903.01329](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01329)
Wei et al. (2022). "Quantum gas microscopy of Kardar-Parisi-Zhang superdiffusion". *Science* 376, 716. [arXiv:2107.00038](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00038)

name: Boundary-driven quantum NESS and matrix products
summary: Boundary-driven Lindblad spin chains are the quantum counterpart of boundary-driven exclusion processes. Their steady states can be solved by matrix-product ansätze like Derrida's ASEP solution, giving exact currents and quantum NESS phase diagrams.
sources: Prosen (2011). "Exact Nonequilibrium Steady State of a Strongly Driven Open XXZ Chain". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107, 137201. [arXiv:1106.2978](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.2978)

Derrida et al. (1993). "Exact solution of a 1D asymmetric exclusion model using a matrix formulation". *J. Phys. A* 26, 1493. [doi:10.1088/0305-4470/26/7/011](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/26/7/011)

name: Transport coefficients from scattering cross sections
summary: The Boltzmann collision integral takes its input from quantum scattering theory: dσ/dΩ fixes the mean free path, and Chapman–Enskog transport cross sections fix viscosity and conductivity. In ultracold gases the s-wave σ=8πa² sets thermalization and evaporative cooling.

name: ETH implies the fluctuation–dissipation theorem
summary: The smooth function f_O(E,ω) in the ETH ansatz fixes both the spectral function and the symmetrized correlator of O. Their ratio is the equilibrium FDT at the temperature of the eigenstate, so single eigenstates satisfy the FDT.
sources: D'Alessio et al. (2016). "From quantum chaos and eigenstate thermalization to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics". *Adv. Phys.* 65, 239. [arXiv:1509.06411](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06411)

name: Thermal noise and cooling of mechanical oscillators
summary: A mechanical resonator's thermal force noise follows from the FDT applied to its susceptibility, and cavity sideband cooling engineers a colder effective bath. The asymmetry between Stokes and anti-Stokes sidebands (∝ n̄+1 vs n̄) is the quantum FDT, used as a primary thermometer.
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: Quantum FDT and the standard quantum limit
summary: The quantum FDT, with ħω coth(ħω/2k_BT) in place of 2k_BT, gives zero-point noise that sets the standard quantum limit of linear amplifiers and interferometers. Squeezing redistributes this noise between quadratures and cannot remove it.
sources: Callen & Welton (1951). "Irreversibility and Generalized Noise". *Phys. Rev.* 83, 34. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.83.34](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.83.34)
Clerk et al. (2010). "Introduction to quantum noise, measurement, and amplification". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1155. [arXiv:0810.4729](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.4729)

name: Doppler cooling as Brownian motion in light
summary: Optical molasses is a Langevin system: radiation pressure provides linear friction and random spontaneous-emission recoils provide momentum diffusion. The Einstein relation k_BT=D_p/α gives the Doppler limit k_BT_D=ħΓ/2.

name: Caldeira–Leggett: quantum Brownian motion
summary: A particle linearly coupled to an Ohmic bath of oscillators obeys the classical Langevin equation at high T, but in quantum form it decoheres spatial superpositions at a rate ∝ γ(Δx/λ_th)². Classical friction and quantum decoherence come from one bath spectral density.
sources: Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Path integral approach to quantum Brownian motion". *Physica A* 121, 587. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4)

name: Lindblad equation as the quantum master equation
summary: The Lindblad equation is the quantum version of the Pauli master equation and Fokker–Planck dynamics. Its diagonal part in the energy basis is a classical rate equation with detailed balance, and quantum trajectories are a stochastic unravelling like Langevin paths.

name: Kramers escape and instanton tunnelling rates
summary: Kramers' thermal escape rate and the Langer–Coleman–Caldeira–Leggett imaginary-time instanton rate are two limits of one rate theory. Below the crossover temperature T_0=ħω_b/2πk_B, macroscopic quantum tunnelling replaces activation, as observed in Josephson junctions.
sources: Hänggi, Talkner & Borkovec (1990). "Reaction-rate theory: fifty years after Kramers". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 62, 251. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.62.251](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.62.251)
Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Path integral approach to quantum Brownian motion". *Physica A* 121, 587. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4)

name: Quantum-jump stochastic thermodynamics
summary: Unravelling Lindblad dynamics into quantum-jump trajectories assigns heat to each emitted or absorbed quantum. Full-counting statistics of these currents obey Gallavotti–Cohen symmetries and TURs (with quantum corrections), mirroring classical stochastic thermodynamics.
sources: Esposito, Harbola & Mukamel (2008). "Nonequilibrium fluctuations, fluctuation theorems, and counting statistics in quantum systems". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1665. [arXiv:0811.3717](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.3717)

name: Quantum fluctuation theorems
summary: Jarzynski and Crooks relations hold for closed quantum systems when work is defined by two projective energy measurements. Strong coupling and coherence complicate the definition of heat.
sources: Esposito, Harbola & Mukamel (2008). "Nonequilibrium fluctuations, fluctuation theorems, and counting statistics in quantum systems". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1665. [arXiv:0811.3717](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.3717)
Jarzynski (1997). "Nonequilibrium Equality for Free Energy Differences". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 78, 2690. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2690](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2690)

name: Kibble–Zurek measurement of BEC critical exponents
summary: Quenching a homogeneous Bose gas through T_c freezes in defects and coherence domains whose size scales as τ_Q^{ν/(1+zν)}. This measured ν≈0.5 and z≈1.4 in homogeneous gases, and trapped-gas correlation-length measurements gave ν≈0.67 (3D XY).
sources: Navon et al. (2015). "Critical dynamics of spontaneous symmetry breaking in a homogeneous Bose gas". *Science* 347, 167. [arXiv:1410.8487](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.8487)

name: Entanglement entropy at quantum critical points
summary: At a 1+1D quantum critical point the ground-state entanglement entropy grows as (c/3) ln L, so the central charge that labels the universality class can be read off from entanglement. Gapped phases obey an area law instead.
sources: Calabrese & Cardy (2004). "Entanglement entropy and quantum field theory". *J. Stat. Mech.* P06002. [arXiv:hep-th/0405152](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405152)
Vidal et al. (2002). "Entanglement in quantum critical phenomena". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 90, 227902. [arXiv:quant-ph/0211074](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0211074)

name: Cold atoms as analog simulators of lattice models
summary: Bose–Hubbard and Fermi–Hubbard models in optical lattices realize lattice models from statistical mechanics with tunable couplings, including the superfluid–Mott transition and antiferromagnetic Ising and Heisenberg correlations. Quantum gas microscopes measure spin correlations site by site.
sources: Greiner et al. (2002). "Quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator in a gas of ultracold atoms". *Nature* 415, 39. [doi:10.1038/415039a](https://doi.org/10.1038/415039a)

name: Rydberg and ion arrays as programmable Ising magnets
summary: Rydberg-blockade tweezer arrays and trapped-ion chains implement transverse-field and long-range Ising models with hundreds of spins. Slow sweeps through their quantum critical points measure Kibble–Zurek scaling, which gives ν and z.
sources: Ebadi et al. (2021). "Quantum phases of matter on a 256-atom programmable quantum simulator". *Nature* 595, 227. [arXiv:2012.12281](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12281)
Keesling et al. (2019). "Quantum Kibble–Zurek mechanism and critical dynamics on a programmable Rydberg simulator". *Nature* 568, 207. [arXiv:1809.05540](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.05540)

name: Quantum–classical mapping: TFIM ↔ (d+1)D Ising
summary: Suzuki–Trotter decomposition maps the d-dimensional transverse-field Ising model at T=0 onto an anisotropic (d+1)-dimensional classical Ising model. The quantum critical point therefore sits in the (d+1)D Ising class, with imaginary time acting as an extra dimension and z=1.
map: e^{-\beta H_{TFIM}}\to\prod e^{K_\tau s_{i,\tau}s_{i,\tau+1}+K s_{i,\tau}s_{j,\tau}},\ \tanh K_\tau=e^{-2\Delta\tau\Gamma}
sources: Suzuki (1976). "Relationship between d-Dimensional Quantal Spin Systems and (d+1)-Dimensional Ising Systems". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 56, 1454. [doi:10.1143/PTP.56.1454](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.56.1454)

name: Gross–Pitaevskii and BCS–BEC crossover as mean field
summary: The Gross–Pitaevskii equation is the Hartree mean-field theory of a condensate, with the macroscopic wavefunction as Landau order parameter. For fermions, BCS mean-field theory with a self-consistent chemical potential interpolates from BCS pairs to molecular BEC across a Feshbach resonance.
breaks: GP mean field fails in 1D and near unitarity, where fluctuations and beyond-mean-field (Lee–Huang–Yang) corrections matter.
sources: Dalfovo et al. (1998). "Theory of Bose-Einstein condensation in trapped gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 71, 463. [arXiv:cond-mat/9806038](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9806038)

name: Dicke superradiance as an exact mean-field transition
summary: Atoms coupled to one cavity mode interact all-to-all, so the Dicke/Hepp–Lieb superradiant transition is mean-field exact. A BEC in a pumped cavity realized it as self-organization into a checkerboard lattice, an open-system phase transition with a Landau order parameter ⟨a⟩.
sources: Baumann et al. (2010). "Dicke quantum phase transition with a superfluid gas in an optical cavity". *Nature* 464, 1301. [doi:10.1038/nature09009](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09009)

name: BKT transition in 2D atomic gases
summary: Quasi-2D trapped Bose gases show the BKT transition directly: interference contrast reveals quasi-long-range phase coherence below T_BKT, and free vortices proliferate above it. Uniform-box gases later confirmed the universal superfluid-density jump.
sources: Hadzibabic et al. (2006). "Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless crossover in a trapped atomic gas". *Nature* 441, 1118. [arXiv:cond-mat/0605291](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0605291)

Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)

name: The four laws of black-hole mechanics
summary: Stationary black holes obey laws formally identical to the four laws of thermodynamics, with surface gravity as temperature and area as entropy. Hawking radiation made the identification physical, because κ really is a temperature of order ħκ/2πck_B.
map: dM=\frac{\kappa}{8\pi G}dA+\Omega_HdJ+\Phi_HdQ\ \leftrightarrow\ dU=TdS+\cdots;\ T_H=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi ck_B},\ S=\frac{k_Bc^3A}{4G\hbar}
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)
Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)
Wald (2001). "The Thermodynamics of Black Holes". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 4, 6. [arXiv:gr-qc/9912119](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9912119)

name: Generalized second law and negative heat capacity
summary: Bekenstein's generalized second law, d(S_outside+S_BH)≥0, extends the second law to horizons. A Schwarzschild black hole has negative heat capacity, C=-8πGM²k_B/ħc, so it heats up as it evaporates.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)

name: Tolman–Ehrenfest: temperature in a gravitational field
summary: In thermal equilibrium in a static spacetime, temperature is not uniform. The local temperature satisfies T√(-g_00)=const, so heat has weight and the zeroth law is modified by redshift. This is used for stellar and neutron-star interiors and is the local form of Hawking temperature redshifting.
sources: Tolman (1930). "On the Weight of Heat and Thermal Equilibrium in General Relativity". *Phys. Rev.* 35, 904. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.35.904](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.35.904)

name: Einstein's equations as an equation of state
summary: Jacobson derived Einstein's equations by imposing the Clausius relation δQ=TdS on every local Rindler horizon, using the Unruh temperature and area-entropy. This suggests that gravity is thermodynamics of underlying microscopic degrees of freedom; entropic-gravity proposals build on the idea but are contested.
map:
\delta Q=T\,dS,\ T= rac{\hbar a}{2\pi},\ S=\eta A\ \Rightarrow\ G_{\mu
u}+\Lambda g_{\mu
u}= rac{2\pi}{\hbar\eta}T_{\mu
u}
sources: Jacobson (1995). "Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1260. [arXiv:gr-qc/9504004](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9504004)

name: Black-hole chemistry: van der Waals-like P–V criticality
summary: With Λ treated as pressure P=-Λ/8πG and the black-hole mass as enthalpy, charged AdS black holes have a liquid–gas-like coexistence line ending at a critical point with mean-field exponents and a universal ratio P_cv_c/T_c=3/8. Holographic heat engines run cycles in this extended phase space.
breaks: The 'volume' is a thermodynamic conjugate rather than a container volume, there is no microscopic molecular picture, and treating Λ as a variable is itself an assumption. The resemblance to van der Waals extends to the mean-field equation of state only.
sources: Kubizňák & Mann (2012). "P-V criticality of charged AdS black holes". *JHEP* 07, 033. [arXiv:1205.0559](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0559)

name: Replica trick from spin glasses to replica wormholes
summary: The Page curve was computed by the replica trick: Rényi entropies Tr ρ^n from gravitational path integrals on n-fold covers, with replica wormholes as new saddles, then continued to n→1. The same analytic continuation in replica number powers spin-glass theory (n→0 for ⟨ln Z⟩).
sources: Penington et al. (2019). "Replica wormholes and the black hole interior". [arXiv:1911.11977](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.11977)
Almheiri et al. (2019). "Replica wormholes and the entropy of Hawking radiation". [arXiv:1911.12333](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.12333)
Parisi (1979). "Infinite Number of Order Parameters for Spin-Glasses". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 43, 1754. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1754](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1754)

name: Euclidean gravity partition function
summary: Gibbons and Hawking computed black-hole thermodynamics from a canonical partition function: the Euclidean action of the black hole, smooth only if imaginary time has period ħ/k_BT_H, gives F=-k_BT ln Z and the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy. Negative heat capacity makes the flat-space canonical ensemble unstable unless the system is boxed (York) or in AdS.
map: Z=\int\mathcal Dg\,e^{-I_E[g]/\hbar}\approx e^{-I_E^{\text{cl}}},\ I_E=\beta M/2\Rightarrow S=\beta M-I_E=A/4G
sources: Gibbons & Hawking (1977). "Action integrals and partition functions in quantum gravity". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2752. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752)

name: LQG black-hole entropy from counting punctures
summary: In loop quantum gravity, horizon microstates are spin-network punctures carrying area quanta. Microcanonical counting gives S∝A, matching A/4 only for a specific Barbero–Immirzi parameter, with a universal -(3/2)ln A correction.
sources: Ashtekar et al. (1998). "Quantum Geometry and Black Hole Entropy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 904. [arXiv:gr-qc/9710007](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9710007)

name: Unruh effect: the vacuum as a Gibbs state
summary: Restricted to a Rindler wedge, the Minkowski vacuum is exactly a thermal density matrix of the boost generator (Bisognano–Wichmann), satisfying the KMS condition at T_U=ħa/2πck_B. Accelerated detectors respond with detailed-balance ratios e^{-ħω/k_BT_U}. De Sitter and black-hole horizons are thermal for the same reason: periodicity in imaginary time.
sources: Unruh (1976). "Notes on black-hole evaporation". *Phys. Rev. D* 14, 870. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870)
Bisognano & Wichmann (1976). "On the duality condition for quantum fields". *J. Math. Phys.* 17, 303. [doi:10.1063/1.522898](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.522898)

name: Microcanonical counting of black-hole microstates
summary: Strominger and Vafa counted the D-brane bound states with the charges of an extremal black hole and found S=ln Ω=A/4G exactly. It is a microcanonical-ensemble derivation of Bekenstein–Hawking entropy, done via the Cardy formula of the dual 2D CFT.
sources: Strominger & Vafa (1996). "Microscopic Origin of the Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy". *Phys. Lett. B* 379, 99. [arXiv:hep-th/9601029](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9601029)

name: Black holes as information-theoretic objects
summary: The black-hole branch uses information-theoretic entropy throughout: area as coarse-grained entropy, entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation, and the question of unitarity, which is a question about fine-grained (von Neumann) entropy.
sources: Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)

name: Bekenstein–Hawking entropy as missing information
summary: Bekenstein argued from information theory that a horizon must carry entropy proportional to its area, because information falling in is lost to outside observers. S_BH=A/4ℓ_P² is then the largest entropy any region can hold.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)

name: Page curve and the entropy of random states
summary: Page's theorem on the average entanglement entropy of a subsystem of a random pure state (nearly maximal until half the system) gives the Page curve. Unitary evaporation requires the radiation's fine-grained entropy to rise and then fall, unlike Hawking's monotonic thermal result.
sources: Page (1993). "Average entropy of a subsystem". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 1291. [arXiv:gr-qc/9305007](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9305007)
Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)
Penington (2020). "Entanglement wedge reconstruction and the information paradox". *JHEP* 09, 002. [arXiv:1905.08255](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08255)

name: Holographic principle and entropy bounds
summary: Black-hole entropy scaling with area rather than volume led to the Bekenstein bound and to the holographic principle of 't Hooft and Susskind: the number of degrees of freedom in a region is bounded by its boundary area in Planck units. This defeats naive extensive counting at gravitational scales.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)
't Hooft (1993). "Dimensional Reduction in Quantum Gravity". [arXiv:gr-qc/9310026](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9310026)
Susskind (1995). "The World as a Hologram". *J. Math. Phys.* 36, 6377. [arXiv:hep-th/9409089](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9409089)

name: Ryu–Takayanagi: entropy equals minimal area
summary: In AdS/CFT the von Neumann entropy of a boundary region equals the area of the minimal bulk surface anchored on it, divided by 4G. This generalizes Bekenstein–Hawking to arbitrary regions and makes entanglement the building block of geometry.
sources: Ryu & Takayanagi (2006). "Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602. [arXiv:hep-th/0603001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001)

name: Hawking radiation is a Planck spectrum
summary: Bogoliubov mixing of in- and out-modes at a horizon gives exactly Bose–Einstein (Fermi–Dirac for fermions) occupation numbers at T_H, filtered by greybody factors. Evaporation is the Stefan–Boltzmann law applied to a horizon of area A.
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Relativistic kinetic theory and the Jüttner gas
summary: The relativistic Boltzmann equation has the Maxwell–Jüttner distribution as its equilibrium. Covariant kinetic theory underlies relativistic hydrodynamics, early-universe freeze-out and neutrino transport, and how temperature transforms under boosts (Planck–Einstein vs Ott) is still debated.

name: Thermal noise of interferometer test masses
summary: Brownian thermal noise of LIGO mirrors and coatings, often the limiting noise in the most sensitive band, is computed from the fluctuation–dissipation theorem. Levin's direct approach evaluates the dissipated power under a fictitious Gaussian pressure matching the laser beam profile.
sources: Levin (1998). "Internal thermal noise in the LIGO test masses: A direct approach". *Phys. Rev. D* 57, 659. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.57.659](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.57.659)
Callen & Welton (1951). "Irreversibility and Generalized Noise". *Phys. Rev.* 83, 34. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.83.34](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.83.34)

name: Kubo viscosity from horizons: η/s = ħ/4πk_B
summary: The shear viscosity of a strongly coupled plasma follows from the Kubo formula, the low-frequency limit of the stress-tensor retarded correlator, computed holographically as graviton absorption by a horizon. The result η/s=ħ/4πk_B is far below kinetic-theory estimates, which assume quasiparticles with mean free paths.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)

name: Hawking–Page transition and deconfinement
summary: In AdS, thermal radiation and large black holes exchange dominance in a first-order Hawking–Page transition at T~1/ℓ_AdS. Via AdS/CFT this is the confinement/deconfinement transition of the dual large-N gauge theory, with free energy jumping from O(1) to O(N²).
sources: Hawking & Page (1983). "Thermodynamics of black holes in anti-de Sitter space". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 87, 577. [doi:10.1007/BF01208266](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01208266)
Witten (1998). "Anti-de Sitter space, thermal phase transition, and confinement in gauge theories". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 505. [arXiv:hep-th/9803131](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803131)

name: Hagedorn temperature and the string phase transition
summary: String state densities grow exponentially with mass, ρ(m)~e^{m/T_H}, so the canonical partition function diverges at the Hagedorn temperature. This signals a phase transition (an analogue of deconfinement) rather than a true limiting temperature.
sources: Atick & Witten (1988). "The Hagedorn transition and the number of degrees of freedom of string theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 310, 291. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(88)90151-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(88)90151-4)

name: Choptuik critical collapse: universality and scaling
summary: At the threshold of black-hole formation, the final mass scales as M∝(p-p*)^γ with γ≈0.37 independent of the initial-data family. The critical solution is a self-similar attractor with a single unstable mode, so γ=1/λ like ν=1/y_t at an RG fixed point.
breaks: There is no thermal ensemble or fluctuation-driven criticality: it is deterministic PDE dynamics near a codimension-one fixed point, and the 'universality class' depends on the matter model (γ differs for radiation fluids).
sources: Choptuik (1993). "Universality and scaling in gravitational collapse of a massless scalar field". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 9. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9)

name: Holographic RG: the radial direction as scale
summary: In AdS/CFT the radial coordinate is an energy scale. The bulk Hamilton–Jacobi equations for radial evolution are RG flow equations of the boundary theory, and domain walls between AdS regions are RG flows between fixed points, with a holographic c-theorem.
map: \mu\frac{d g_i}{d\mu}=\beta_i(g)\ \leftrightarrow\ \text{radial flow of bulk fields }\phi_i(r),\ r\sim\ln\mu
sources: de Boer, Verlinde & Verlinde (2000). "On the Holographic Renormalization Group". *JHEP* 08, 003. [arXiv:hep-th/9912012](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9912012)

name: Asymptotic safety: a Wilson–Fisher fixed point for gravity
summary: Asymptotic safety applies Wilson's RG to gravity: a non-Gaussian UV fixed point of Newton's coupling with finitely many relevant directions would make gravity predictive, just as a critical fixed point has finitely many relevant scaling fields.

name: Random matrices and localization in the Dirac spectrum
summary: Low-lying eigenvalues of the QCD Dirac operator follow chiral random-matrix theory, and the Banks–Casher relation ties the chiral condensate to the spectral density at zero. Above T_c the low modes localize, with an Anderson-type mobility edge, linking chiral restoration to localization.
sources: Verbaarschot & Wettig (2000). "Random Matrix Theory and Chiral Symmetry in QCD". *Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 50, 343. [arXiv:hep-ph/0003017](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0003017)
Banks & Casher (1980). "Chiral symmetry breaking in confining theories". *Nucl. Phys. B* 169, 103. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(80)90255-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(80)90255-2)

name: Finite-temperature QFT: Matsubara formalism
summary: A thermal QFT is the Euclidean path integral on a spatial manifold times a circle of circumference ħβ, with bosons periodic and fermions antiperiodic. Matsubara frequencies ω_n=2πn/β or (2n+1)π/β turn the grand partition function into diagrammatic perturbation theory.
sources: Matsubara (1955). "A New Approach to Quantum-Statistical Mechanics". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 14, 351. [doi:10.1143/PTP.14.351](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.14.351)

name: Entanglement entropy and the c-theorem
summary: In 1+1D CFT the entanglement entropy of an interval is (c/3) ln(ℓ/a), so the central charge is an entropy coefficient. Strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy gives an entropic proof that c decreases along RG flows.
sources: Calabrese & Cardy (2004). "Entanglement entropy and quantum field theory". *J. Stat. Mech.* P06002. [arXiv:hep-th/0405152](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405152)
Casini & Huerta (2004). "A finite entanglement entropy and the c-theorem". *Phys. Lett. B* 600, 142. [arXiv:hep-th/0405111](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405111)

name: Integrable field theory: Ising in a field and E8
summary: The 2D Ising critical point perturbed by a magnetic field is an integrable massive QFT with eight particles whose masses follow the E8 Lie algebra (m₂/m₁=2cos π/5, the golden ratio). Neutron scattering on the Ising-chain magnet CoNb₂O₆ observed the ratio.
sources: Coldea et al. (2010). "Quantum Criticality in an Ising Chain: Experimental Evidence for Emergent E8 Symmetry". *Science* 327, 177. [arXiv:1103.3694](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3694)

name: Exactly solvable lattice models as CFTs
summary: At criticality, exactly solved 2D models (Ising, Potts, vertex models, XXZ chain) are lattice realizations of conformal field theories. Their exponents are conformal weights, and finite-size spectra of transfer matrices give the central charge and scaling dimensions.
map: E_0(L)=Lf_\infty-\frac{\pi c v}{6L},\ E_n-E_0=\frac{2\pi v}{L}(h+\bar h)
sources: Belavin, Polyakov & Zamolodchikov (1984). "Infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 241, 333. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X)

name: Directed percolation is Reggeon field theory
summary: The field theory of directed percolation is identical to Reggeon field theory, developed in the 1970s for high-energy hadron scattering. Its ε-expansion around d_c=4 transferred directly to absorbing-state transitions.
sources: Cardy & Sugar (1980). "Directed percolation and Reggeon field theory". *J. Phys. A* 13, L423. [doi:10.1088/0305-4470/13/12/002](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/13/12/002)
Hinrichsen (2000). "Non-equilibrium critical phenomena and phase transitions into absorbing states". *Adv. Phys.* 49, 815. [arXiv:cond-mat/0001070](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0001070)

name: Departure from equilibrium in baryogenesis
summary: Sakharov's third condition, departure from thermal equilibrium, is a statement of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: in equilibrium CPT forces ⟨B⟩=0. Leptogenesis yields are computed from coupled Boltzmann equations for heavy-neutrino decays and washout.

name: WIMP freeze-out from the Boltzmann equation
summary: Relic dark-matter abundance comes from a Boltzmann equation in an expanding universe. Annihilation keeps n near equilibrium until the rate n⟨σv⟩ falls below H, after which the comoving density freezes out at Ω h²∝1/⟨σv⟩.
sources: Gondolo & Gelmini (1991). "Cosmic abundances of stable particles: improved analysis". *Nucl. Phys. B* 360, 145. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(91)90438-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(91)90438-4)
Bertone, Hooper & Silk (2005). "Particle dark matter: evidence, candidates and constraints". *Phys. Rep.* 405, 279. [arXiv:hep-ph/0404175](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0404175)

name: Quantum kinetic equations for dense neutrino gases
summary: In supernovae and the early universe, mixing neutrinos are described by a matrix-valued Boltzmann equation (flavour density matrices with collisions). Collective 'fast flavour' instabilities are analysed with linear-response stability theory, as for plasma waves.
sources: Sigl & Raffelt (1993). "General kinetic description of relativistic mixed neutrinos". *Nucl. Phys. B* 406, 423. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(93)90175-O](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(93)90175-O)
Fiorillo & Raffelt (2024). "Theory of neutrino fast flavor evolution. Part I. Linear response theory and stability conditions". *JHEP*. [arXiv:2406.06708](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06708)

name: Dispersion relations for hadronic vacuum polarization
summary: Causality and analyticity of the photon vacuum-polarization function give a Kramers–Kronig-type dispersion integral over σ(e⁺e⁻→hadrons). It is the data-driven route to the leading hadronic contribution to muon g−2, the same structure as the susceptibility relations of linear response.
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: Parton showers as Markov processes
summary: A parton shower is a Markov chain in an evolution variable. The Sudakov factor is the no-emission survival probability of a non-homogeneous Poisson process, and DGLAP evolution is a master equation for parton densities, so showers are sampled with veto algorithms from stochastic simulation.
sources: Sjöstrand et al. (2015). "An introduction to PYTHIA 8.2". *Comput. Phys. Commun.* 191, 159. [arXiv:1410.3012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3012)

name: Stochastic quantization and Hybrid Monte Carlo
summary: Parisi–Wu stochastic quantization obtains the Euclidean QFT measure e^{-S} as the equilibrium of Langevin dynamics in a fictitious time. Hybrid Monte Carlo, which combines molecular dynamics, momentum refreshment and a Metropolis test, is the workhorse algorithm of lattice QCD.

name: Euclidean QFT as statistical field theory
summary: Euclidean QFT in D dimensions is classical statistical mechanics of fields in D dimensions, with e^{-S_E/ħ} as Boltzmann weight. Particle-physics tools (Feynman diagrams, renormalization, instantons) and stat-mech tools (Monte Carlo, high-T expansions, RG) are interchangeable.

name: Critical points are conformal field theories
summary: At a continuous transition, scale invariance plus locality enhances to conformal invariance. The fixed point is a CFT whose operator dimensions are the critical exponents and whose OPE data fix all correlations.

name: Statistical field theory ↔ renormalizable QFT
summary: Landau–Ginzburg–Wilson field theory of a critical point is a Euclidean φ⁴ QFT. The correlation length plays the role of inverse mass, and the continuum limit at T_c is a renormalized massless QFT.

name: Electroweak crossover at T ~ 160 GeV
summary: Electroweak symmetry is restored at high temperature. Dimensional reduction to a 3D SU(2)-Higgs theory and lattice simulations show that for m_h=125 GeV the transition is a smooth crossover, beyond the endpoint (in the 3D Ising class) of the first-order line. Standard-Model electroweak baryogenesis is therefore ruled out.

name: Conformal bootstrap determinations of exponents
summary: Conformal bootstrap constraints (crossing symmetry plus unitarity) fix the 3D Ising, O(N) and other critical exponents to the highest precision available, ν≈0.62999 and η≈0.03630 for Ising, beyond Monte Carlo and the ε-expansion.
sources: El-Showk et al. (2012). "Solving the 3D Ising Model with the Conformal Bootstrap". *Phys. Rev. D* 86, 025022. [arXiv:1203.6064](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.6064)

name: Pisarski–Wilczek: universality of the chiral transition
summary: With symmetry and an ε-expansion, the QCD chiral transition with two massless flavours is in the 3D O(4) class, while with three massless flavours it must be first order (no infrared-stable fixed point). Physical quark masses turn it into a crossover at T_c≈156 MeV, with O(4) scaling still visible in lattice data.
map: SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R\simeq O(4)\Rightarrow\text{3D }O(4)\ \text{class};\ N_f=3:\ \text{cubic invariant}\Rightarrow\text{first order}
sources: Pisarski & Wilczek (1984). "Remarks on the chiral phase transition in chromodynamics". *Phys. Rev. D* 29, 338. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.29.338](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.29.338)

name: 2D Ising as the c=1/2 minimal model
summary: The 2D Ising critical point is the M(4,3) minimal CFT with c=1/2. Its primaries σ (h=1/16) and ε (h=1/2) give η=1/4 and ν=1 exactly. In 3D the bootstrap places Ising at a kink on the boundary of allowed (Δ_σ, Δ_ε).
sources: Belavin, Polyakov & Zamolodchikov (1984). "Infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 241, 333. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X)
El-Showk et al. (2012). "Solving the 3D Ising Model with the Conformal Bootstrap". *Phys. Rev. D* 86, 025022. [arXiv:1203.6064](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.6064)

name: Svetitsky–Yaffe: deconfinement in Z_N spin-model classes
summary: With the Polyakov loop as order parameter for center symmetry, a continuous deconfinement transition of a (d+1)-dimensional SU(N) gauge theory falls in the universality class of a d-dimensional Z_N spin model. Pure SU(2) in 3+1D deconfines in the 3D Ising class.
sources: Svetitsky & Yaffe (1982). "Critical behavior at finite-temperature confinement transitions". *Nucl. Phys. B* 210, 423. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(82)90172-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(82)90172-9)

name: Lattice gauge theory as statistical mechanics
summary: Wilson's lattice QCD is a statistical-mechanics model of group-valued link variables. Wegner's Z₂ lattice gauge theory is its Ising prototype with no local order parameter, strong-coupling expansions are high-temperature expansions, and Monte Carlo importance sampling carried over directly.
sources: Wilson (1974). "Confinement of quarks". *Phys. Rev. D* 10, 2445. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445)
Wegner (1971). "Duality in Generalized Ising Models and Phase Transitions without Local Order Parameters". *J. Math. Phys.* 12, 2259. [doi:10.1063/1.1665530](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1665530)
Creutz (1980). "Monte Carlo study of quantized SU(2) gauge theory". *Phys. Rev. D* 21, 2308. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.21.2308](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.21.2308)

name: Higgs potential as a Landau–Ginzburg free energy
summary: The Higgs potential has the Landau form with a sign-changing quadratic term. Its vacuum is spontaneously broken order, and coupling to gauge fields gives the Higgs–Anderson mechanism already known from Ginzburg–Landau superconductors.
sources: Englert & Brout (1964). "Broken Symmetry and the Mass of Gauge Vector Mesons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 321. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

name: NJL: BCS mean field for chiral symmetry breaking
summary: Nambu and Jona-Lasinio modelled nucleon mass generation explicitly on the BCS gap equation. The constituent mass is a self-consistent mean field from a four-fermion attraction, with pions as Goldstone modes, and the NJL model remains a mean-field tool for QCD phase diagrams.
sources: Nambu & Jona-Lasinio (1961). "Dynamical Model of Elementary Particles Based on an Analogy with Superconductivity. I". *Phys. Rev.* 122, 345. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.122.345](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.122.345)

name: Hierarchy problem as tuning to a critical point
summary: The Higgs mass term is the one relevant operator of the Standard Model. Keeping m_h ≪ Λ requires fine-tuning the bare parameter close to its critical value, just as a magnet must be tuned to T_c for ξ≫a. Naturalness asks what symmetry or dynamics does the tuning.
breaks: A magnet is tuned by an experimenter or by self-organized dynamics. For the Higgs no tuning agent is known (anthropics, SUSY, compositeness and relaxion proposals are all speculative), and the UV cutoff Λ may not exist physically.
sources: Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: Wilsonian EFT: irrelevant operators and decoupling
summary: Effective field theory is the RG statement that operators of dimension above D are irrelevant, suppressed by (E/Λ)^{Δ-D}. Decoupling of heavy physics in particle physics and universality at critical points are the same fact.
sources: Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)
Weinberg (1979). "Phenomenological Lagrangians". *Physica A* 96, 327. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1)

name: Wilson's RG unifies running couplings and critical exponents
summary: QFT beta functions and the critical-phenomena RG are the same flow in theory space. A Wilson–Fisher fixed point is a zero of β(u), and the anomalous dimensions there are critical exponents, computed by the same diagrams in the ε-expansion.
sources: Wilson (1971). "Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena. I. Renormalization Group and the Kadanoff Scaling Picture". *Phys. Rev. B* 4, 3174. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3174](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3174)
Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: BKT, Coulomb gas and sine-Gordon duality
summary: The 2D XY vortex gas maps onto the 2D Coulomb gas and the sine-Gordon field theory, which Coleman showed is dual to the massive Thirring model. The Kosterlitz RG equations are the sine-Gordon beta functions, and β²=8π is the BKT point.
sources: Coleman (1975). "Quantum sine-Gordon equation as the massive Thirring model". *Phys. Rev. D* 11, 2088. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.11.2088](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.11.2088)

Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)

name: Reactors as heat sources for Rankine cycles
summary: Fission reactors and fusion plants are heat sources whose electrical efficiency (~33% for LWRs, more for high-temperature designs) is bounded by Carnot at the coolant outlet temperature and achieved with Rankine or Brayton cycles. Decay heat after shutdown is a thermodynamic safety problem.

name: Nuclear liquid–gas transition and the QCD phase diagram
summary: Strongly interacting matter has two first-order lines ending in Ising-class critical points: the nuclear liquid–gas transition (T_c≈15–18 MeV, near saturation density, from van der Waals-like nucleon interactions) and the conjectured chiral/deconfinement line at high μ_B. Multifragmentation caloric curves show a liquid–gas plateau, and coexistence follows the Gibbs conditions in (T, μ_B).
sources: Pochodzalla et al. (1995). "Probing the Nuclear Liquid-Gas Phase Transition". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1040. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1040](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1040)
Du et al. (2025). "The QCD phase diagram and Beam Energy Scan physics: A theory overview". [arXiv:2402.10183](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10183)

name: Nuclear statistical equilibrium and the deuterium bottleneck
summary: Early-universe abundances follow the Saha/law-of-mass-action equation μ_A=Zμ_p+Nμ_n. Deuterium is suppressed until T≈0.07 MeV, well below its 2.2 MeV binding energy, because the photon-to-baryon ratio η⁻¹~10⁹ is huge (entropy wins).
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Gibbs vs Maxwell constructions and nuclear pasta
summary: With two conserved charges (baryon number and electric charge), a first-order hadron–quark or liquid–gas transition in a star can form a mixed phase under the Gibbs conditions instead of a sharp Maxwell interface. In the inner crust, Coulomb frustration of phase separation produces 'pasta' phases (rods, slabs).
sources: Glendenning (1992). "First-order phase transitions with more than one conserved charge: Consequences for neutron stars". *Phys. Rev. D* 46, 1274. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.46.1274](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.46.1274)
Ravenhall, Pethick & Wilson (1983). "Structure of Matter below Nuclear Saturation Density". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 50, 2066. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.2066](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.2066)

name: r-process waiting points as Saha equilibrium
summary: In the hot, neutron-rich r-process, (n,γ)⇌(γ,n) equilibrium along each isotopic chain is a Saha equation. Neutron density and temperature fix the waiting-point nuclei through their neutron separation energies, and β-decays then move material to higher Z.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Liquid-drop model: nuclei as droplets of nuclear liquid
summary: The semi-empirical mass formula is the leptodermous (volume plus surface) expansion of a droplet of saturated, incompressible liquid. The volume term is the bulk chemical potential, and the surface term is a surface tension σ≈1 MeV/fm², the same capillarity that sets nucleation barriers.
map: B=a_VA-a_SA^{2/3}-\cdots\ \leftrightarrow\ G=-\Delta\mu N+4\pi r^2\sigma,\ a_S=4\pi r_0^2\sigma
breaks: Nuclei have only ~10–300 constituents, so curvature and shell corrections (magic numbers) are comparable to surface terms. The 'liquid' is a quantum Fermi liquid with pairing, not a classical van der Waals fluid.
sources: Weizsäcker (1935). "Zur Theorie der Kernmassen". *Z. Phys.* 96, 431. [doi:10.1007/BF01337700](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01337700)
Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)

name: Random-matrix theory born in compound nuclei
summary: Wigner introduced random matrices to model the dense resonances of compound nuclei. Level-spacing repulsion (Wigner surmise) and Porter–Thomas width distributions became, after Dyson's classification, a core tool of disordered and complex systems: mesoscopic transport, localization and spin glasses.
sources: Wigner (1955). "Characteristic Vectors of Bordered Matrices With Infinite Dimensions". *Ann. Math.* 62, 548. [doi:10.2307/1970079](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970079)

name: Colour-string percolation as a deconfinement model
summary: In string-percolation models, colour flux tubes from nucleon–nucleon collisions overlap as discs in the transverse plane. Deconfinement is identified with 2D continuum percolation of these discs at a critical density, which predicts the onset of collective effects with centrality.
breaks: Percolation is purely geometric and has no thermodynamics; the QCD transition at μ_B=0 is an analytic crossover with no diverging length. Connectivity of strings is not equivalent to deconfinement or thermalization.
sources: Satz (2000). "Colour deconfinement in nuclear collisions". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 63, 1511. [arXiv:hep-ph/0007069](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0007069)

name: Baryon-number cumulants as grand-canonical susceptibilities
summary: Lattice QCD and heavy-ion phenomenology use the grand-canonical relation between pressure derivatives and conserved-charge fluctuations: χ_n^B are cumulants of net baryon number. Real μ_B gives a complex Boltzmann weight (the sign problem), so lattice works by Taylor expansion or imaginary μ. Experiment must correct for global charge conservation, a canonical-ensemble effect.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)
Du et al. (2025). "The QCD phase diagram and Beam Energy Scan physics: A theory overview". [arXiv:2402.10183](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10183)

name: Statistical hadronization and the thermal model
summary: Hadron yields across species and collision energies follow a grand-canonical hadron-resonance-gas partition function with just T_ch≈156 MeV and μ_B(√s), which coincides with the lattice crossover. In small systems strangeness is suppressed because exact canonical conservation, not grand-canonical averaging, applies (ensemble inequivalence).
sources: Andronic et al. (2018). "Decoding the phase structure of QCD via particle production at high energy". *Nature* 561, 321. [arXiv:1710.09425](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.09425)

name: Compound-nucleus decay as microcanonical evaporation
summary: Bohr's compound nucleus 'forgets' how it formed and decays statistically. Weisskopf evaporation and Hauser–Feshbach theory compute decay widths from detailed balance and level densities, so emission spectra are Maxwellian with a nuclear temperature T=(∂ln ρ/∂E)^{-1}. This is microcanonical statistical mechanics of a ~100-body system.
sources: Weisskopf (1937). "Statistics and Nuclear Reactions". *Phys. Rev.* 52, 295. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.52.295](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.52.295)
Hauser & Feshbach (1952). "The Inelastic Scattering of Neutrons". *Phys. Rev.* 87, 366. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.87.366](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.87.366)

name: Parton entanglement entropy at small x
summary: Kharzeev and Levin proposed that the entanglement entropy between probed and unprobed regions of a proton at small x is S=ln(xG(x)), saturating the maximum for a dipole cascade. Hadron multiplicities measured in DIS are then compared with this entropy.
sources: Kharzeev & Levin (2017). "Deep inelastic scattering as a probe of entanglement". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 114008. [arXiv:1702.03489](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03489)

name: Richardson's exact solution of the pairing model
summary: The reduced BCS pairing Hamiltonian for a finite set of levels is exactly solvable by Bethe-ansatz-type Richardson equations (Richardson–Gaudin integrability). It describes pairing in nuclei and ultrasmall superconducting grains beyond mean field, where BCS breaks down as Δ approaches the level spacing.
sources: Richardson (1963). "A restricted class of exact eigenstates of the pairing-force Hamiltonian". *Phys. Lett.* 3, 277. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(63)90259-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(63)90259-2)

name: Stefan–Boltzmann limit of the quark–gluon gas
summary: An ideal QGP is a relativistic Bose (gluons) plus Fermi (quarks) gas, ε/T⁴=(π²/30)(16+(21/2)n_f), and the jump in degrees of freedom across T_c signals deconfinement. Lattice EOS reaches only ~80% of this at a few T_c, a sign of strong coupling.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)

name: Neutron degeneracy pressure and β-equilibrium
summary: Neutron-star matter is a degenerate Fermi system. Oppenheimer and Volkoff found that an ideal neutron Fermi gas supports at most ~0.7 M_⊙, and the observed 2 M_⊙ stars require repulsive interactions. Equilibrium composition follows from μ_n=μ_p+μ_e at T≈0.
sources: Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)

name: Fermi-gas nuclear level densities
summary: Bethe's level-density formula treats the nucleus as a degenerate Fermi gas. The Sommerfeld expansion gives E*=aT² and S=2aT, so ρ(E)∝exp(2√(aE)) with a≈A/8 MeV⁻¹. These level densities feed Hauser–Feshbach rates for reactors and the r-process.
sources: Bethe (1936). "An Attempt to Calculate the Number of Energy Levels of a Heavy Nucleus". *Phys. Rev.* 50, 332. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.50.332](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.50.332)

name: Chain reactions as critical branching processes
summary: A neutron chain reaction is a Galton–Watson branching process, and criticality k_eff=1 is its critical point, mean-field directed percolation (an absorbing-state transition with the zero population absorbing). Reactor-noise methods (Feynman-α, Rossi-α) use the diverging fluctuations near k=1 to measure subcriticality.
sources: Ryazanov (2026). "Multifractality, percolation threshold and critical point of a nuclear reactor". [arXiv:2601.03399](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03399)
Hinrichsen (2000). "Non-equilibrium critical phenomena and phase transitions into absorbing states". *Adv. Phys.* 49, 815. [arXiv:cond-mat/0001070](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0001070)

name: Gluon saturation as FKPP travelling fronts
summary: The Balitsky–Kovchegov equation for gluon saturation is in the universality class of the FKPP reaction–diffusion equation, so the saturation scale is the position of a pulled front in ln(1/x) and geometric scaling is front translation. Noise corrections (Brunet–Derrida) carry over from front-propagation statistics.
sources: Munier & Peschanski (2003). "Geometric scaling as traveling waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 91, 232001. [arXiv:hep-ph/0309177](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0309177)

name: Neutron transport is a linear Boltzmann equation
summary: Reactor physics solves the linear Boltzmann transport equation for neutron angular flux, with scattering, absorption and fission sources. Its P₁/diffusion approximation (Fick's law, diffusion length) and Fermi age theory of moderation are Chapman–Enskog-type reductions.

name: From kinetic theory to viscous relativistic hydrodynamics
summary: Second-order (Israel–Stewart) viscous hydrodynamics, the standard model of heavy-ion flow, is derived from the relativistic Boltzmann equation by Grad's moment method. Hadronic afterburners (UrQMD, SMASH) are Boltzmann transport, and the hydro-to-kinetic switch uses Cooper–Frye sampling of a local Jüttner distribution.
sources: Israel & Stewart (1979). "Transient relativistic thermodynamics and kinetic theory". *Ann. Phys.* 118, 341. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(79)90130-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(79)90130-1)

name: Neutron–proton freeze-out as rate competition
summary: The n/p ratio tracks its equilibrium value e^{-Q/T} until weak rates Γ∝G_F²T⁵ fall below the Hubble rate H∝T²/M_Pl at T_f≈0.8 MeV. That fixes Y_p≈0.25, a textbook example of kinetic freeze-out from a Boltzmann rate equation.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Gamow peak: Maxwell–Boltzmann tail times tunnelling
summary: Thermonuclear reaction rates are Maxwell–Boltzmann averages of the cross section. The falling exponential tail times the rising Gamow tunnelling factor gives a sharp peak at E₀ ≫ k_BT, so stellar burning and fusion-plasma reactivities ⟨σv⟩ sample only the far tail of the distribution.
sources: Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)
